# Movie dataset

This dataset is taken from the package `ggplot2movies`. [link to the
description
online](https://vincentarelbundock.github.io/Rdatasets/doc/ggplot2movies/movies.html)

## The data

There are various ways to use the data from this package. We can load it
as `ggplot2movies::movies`, however, this does not store it as a
variable in our environment. So, we can assign it to a variable or we
can load it using `data` to store it as a variable.

```{r store data as an object, include = FALSE}
movies <- ggplot2movies::movies
```

## Data exploration

```{r initial exploration, echo = TRUE}
head(clean_movies)
dim(clean_movies)
glimpse(clean_movies)
class(clean_movies)
```

The data contains:

- 58,788 movies (rows)

- 24 columns:

  - Movie title
  - Year
  - Length (minutes)
  - Budget
  - Rating
  - Votes
  - r1-10 (percentile per score 1-10, rounded to nearest 10%)
  - MPAA rating
  - Genre (action, animation, comedy, drama, documentary, romance,
    short)

## Data tidying and transformation 

We tidy the data by:

- trimming whitespaces

- saving as a tibble

- Eliminating the variables "budget" and "mpaa". These contain many
  `NAs` and empty characters, which is why we did not consider them.

- made sure all numeric variables were considered as numeric

- introducing the possibility of filtering movies that have votes higher
  than a certain number

```{r transform the data }
# A cutoff of on the first quartile
cutoff_votes <- 0

#Create a new clean dataset
clean_movies <- movies |>   
  map(~str_trim(.x)) |>   
  as_tibble() |> 
  select(-budget, -mpaa) |> 
  mutate_at(vars(-title), as.numeric) |>  
  filter(votes >= cutoff_votes)|> 
  mutate(decade = if_else(year %in% seq(2000,2005, 1), paste0(year  %/% 10 * 10),
                  if_else(year %in% seq(1900, 1909, 1), paste0("190",(year - 1900) %/% 10 * 10), 
                  if_else(year %in% seq(1910, 1999, 1), paste0("19",(year - 1900) %/% 10 * 10), 
                          "1890")))) |> arrange (year) |> 
  mutate_at(vars(decade), as.numeric)

mean_ratings_decade <- clean_movies |> 
  group_by(decade) |> 
  mutate(mean_rating_decade = mean(rating)) 

by_decades <- clean_movies |> group_by(decade)

overview_decades <- by_decades |> tally(name = "number of movies") 
```

```{r save as R objects}
#Save clean datasets 
saveRDS(clean_movies, "shiny_sanne/data/clean_movies.rds")
saveRDS(overview_decades, "shiny_sanne/data/movies_per_decade.rds")
```

## Data manipulation

The genre variables appear to be binary, but are loaded in as integers.

We have 7 rows indicating the genre of a movie, movies can have multiple
genres.

## Analysis plan

- We have a group of variables for the distribution of the rating.
- We have a group of variables for the genres.
- We have ratings and the number of votes.
- We have budget (but lots of NAs)
- We have movie lengths (in minutes)

It would be interesting to see the distribution of the ranks, in
relation to the number of voters. Then, we also have the information on
which year the movie was released.

**Ranks**

- How are the votes distributed (across the r1-10)?
- Can movie length predict scores + how many people watched it.

**Genre**

It would also be interesting to look at the popularity of the genres:

- Which movie genres has the highest overall scores?
- Which movie genre is voted on most (mean across the movies, min + max)
- How long are movies across genres (and does this influence the rank?)

**Decades**

Lastly, we can group per decade

- Which genres were popular along the decades?
- How many votes were there across the decades?
- Ratings across the decades? (overall, per genre)
- Did movie lengths change over the years?

These graphs can all be made interactive, with options for choosing
genres and decades, perhaps also with the possibility to select
double/triple genres (we will look into the distribution of multiple
genres), or to select certain years even (along with certain decades).

- Perhaps make it possible to select your own range of release years.

### Data manipulation

- We have 10 rows for the rating (r1 - r10)
- We have 7 rows indicating the genre of a movie, movies can have
  multiple genres.

Create subsets based on the movie genres

```{r}
clean_movies <- clean_movies |> 
  group_by(year) |> 
  mutate(mean_rating = mean(rating), mean_votes = mean(votes)) 

# add variable decade
clean_movies <- clean_movies  |> 
  mutate(decade = if_else(year %in% seq(2000,2005, 1), paste0(year  %/% 10 * 10),
                  if_else(year %in% seq(1900, 1909, 1), paste0("190",(year - 1900) %/% 10 * 10), 
                  if_else(year %in% seq(1910, 1999, 1), paste0("19",(year - 1900) %/% 10 * 10), 
                          "1890")))) |> arrange (year) 

clean_movies$decade <- as.numeric(clean_movies$decade)

mean_ratings_decade <- clean_movies |> 
  group_by(decade) |> 
  mutate(mean_rating_decade = mean(rating)) 

by_decades <- clean_movies |> group_by(decade)

overview_decades <- by_decades |> tally(name = "number of movies")


saveRDS(clean_movies, "clean_movies.rds")
saveRDS(clean_movies, "shiny_sanne/data/clean_movies.rds")
saveRDS(overview_decades, "shiny_sanne/data/movies_per_decade.rds")
```

## Summary statistics

In the following table, basic statistics for the relevant numerical
variables in the dataset are summarised

```{r}
movies %>% 
  select(2:6) %>% 
  pivot_longer(everything(), 
               names_to = "variable", 
               values_to ="value") %>%
  group_by(variable) %>% 
  summarise(
    Mean = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    Minimum = min(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    Maximum = max(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    Missing = sum(is.na(value))) %>% 
  gt() %>% 
  fmt_number(columns = c(Mean, Minimum, Maximum, Missing),
             decimals = 2) %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "Movies - Summary statistics"
  )
```

## Visualize data distributions

The distribution of each relevant numerical variable can be visualized
in the following density graphs. These are: year, length, budget,
rating, and number of votes.

```{r}

movies %>% 
  pivot_longer(
  cols = 2:6,   
  names_to = "variable",      
  values_to = "value"         
) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = value, fill = variable, colour = variable)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ variable, 
    scales = "free",
  labeller = as_labeller(c(
    "year" = "Year",
    "length"= "Length",
    "budget"= "Budget",
    "rating"= "Rating",
    "votes"= "Number of votes"))) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Density") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) + 
  theme(legend.position = "none")

```

## Visualize rating patterns

We consider the 100 movies with the highest average rating and plot in a
heatmap the percentage of votes awarding 1-10 ratings. This will
visualize whether these top-rated movies have similar distribution
between rating points.

```{r}
library(superheat)

heatmap_rating <- 
  clean_movies %>% 
  select(title, rating, r1:r10) %>% 
  arrange(desc(rating)) %>% 
  slice_head(n = 100) %>% 
  {
    matrix_rating <- as.matrix(select(., r1:r10))
    rownames(matrix_rating) <- .$title
    superheat(
      matrix_rating,
      pretty.order.rows = FALSE,        
      yr = .$rating,                  
      yr.plot.type = "bar",
      yr.axis.name = "Average Rating",
      yr.bar.col = "lightblue4",
      heat.col.scheme = "viridis",
      grid.hline.col = "white",
      grid.vline.col = "white",
      left.label.text.size = 2.5,
      bottom.label.text.angle = 0
    )
  }
```

#### Impact of 10/10 votes on average rating

We also investigate whether the percentage of users who awarded a 10/10
rating (r10 variable) can predict the average rating of a movie.

```{r}
fit_r10 <- 
  lm(rating ~ 1 + r10, 
     data = clean_movies) 

summary(fit_r10)

# Visualise diagnostic plots of the linear model in one figure
plot_lm_r10 <- fit_r10 %>% 
  {par(mfrow = c(2, 2));
    plot(.)}
# no clear violations of the requirements
```

The low p-value and adjusted R\^2 of 0.1789 reveal a correlation,
although weak, between r10 and rating. This can be visualized on the
following scatter plot of the r10 data.

```{r}
r10_rating_plot <- ggplot(
  clean_movies, 
      aes(r10, rating)) +
      geom_point() +
  labs(dictionary = c(
    rating = "Average rating /10",
    r10 = "Percentage of 10/10 votes")) +
  stat_smooth(method = "lm", 
              formula = y ~ 1 + x, 
              se = FALSE, 
              color = "red3", 
              linetype = 1)

print(r10_rating_plot)
```
